artifacts.summary: Designs the feedback mechanism: extend the existing proposed_file_scope channel to implement, sourced mechanically from git-commit-phase.sh's own drop-time computation rather than agent self-report, auto-merged without an operator confirmation gate; confirms all six territory/dependency sibling tasks already landed with no conflicts, including the git-commit-scoped.sh chokepoint (394), which landed as a redundant drop-and-warn gate rather than the refusal the dispatch description speculated about.

memory_candidates.content: Mechanize-over-instructing precedent: git-commit-phase.sh's own header documents a prose 'remember to do X' reminder firing 0/8 times in one measured run versus 16/16 once the identical step moved inside a script every caller must already invoke. When designing a feedback/proposal mechanism that depends on an agent noticing and later self-reporting something (e.g. a dropped file path), prefer sourcing it mechanically from whichever script already computed the fact synchronously, rather than relying on agent self-report of the same fact after the moment has passed.

specs/{N}_{slug}/issues.jsonl is explicitly CAPTURE ONLY (context/formats/issue-log.md): nothing recorded there is ever surfaced mid-run or read back to drive a decision. When a mechanism needs to act on a fact that is ALSO being logged as an issue (e.g. a containment-dropped file path also needing to feed a file_scope proposal), source that fact directly from the computing script's own in-memory value at the moment it happens -- never by reading issues.jsonl back after the fact, even though the data looks present there.

return-metadata-file.md's 'Multiple Sequential Writers' section states a single blanket producer for several top-level fields ('producer-owned by the implementation agent'), but at least one of those fields (proposed_file_scope) has a per-operation producer that varies (the research agent for research; potentially a script like git-commit-phase.sh for implement). When extending a producer-owned .return-meta.json field to a new operation, check whether the field's actual producer is the dispatched AGENT or an auxiliary SCRIPT invoked mid-dispatch -- the read-modify-write obligation on the later writer is the same either way, but documentation describing 'the producer' as a single fixed role can be stale/inconsistent across a schema doc's own sections.
